references.text: Ezra warns the Israelites against seeking peace and prosperity with the pagan nations, reflecting the prohibition in Deuteronomy against seeking the peace and prosperity of the Ammonites and Moabites.
Balaam was hired to curse Israel, which is the background for the prohibition against seeking the welfare of the Moabites and Ammonites.
The Moabites led Israel into sin at Baal-Peor, which is one reason why Israel was not to seek their peace and prosperity.
Nehemiah reads the law that forbids Ammonites and Moabites from entering the assembly of God, and refers to their hostile actions against Israel.
The immediate context explains why Israel was not to seek the peace of the Ammonites and Moabites—they did not meet Israel with food and water, and they hired Balaam to curse them.
